<brief>
Build Cowdie, a playful 3D virtual pet experience inspired by Tamagotchi.

Create a pet that the user can feed and care for. Make it feel alive, expressive, and enjoyable to spend time with. Feeding must be a real interaction with a visible response from the pet.
</brief>

<freedom>
You have full creative control over the features, visual style, pet design, environment, interactions, progression, and technical implementation. Choose what makes the strongest experience. There is no prescribed feature checklist beyond a 3D pet that we can feed and care for like a Tamagotchi.

Build a complete, polished, functional web app. Own the product and design decisions.
</freedom>

Work only inside the current working directory. Do not read, list, search, or edit files outside the current working directory. Treat it as a standalone project root.
During setup, configure your app and package scripts to use port 9359, then use that port for runtime verification.
Use pnpm exclusively if dependency installation or package scripts are needed. Do not use npm.
Set the browser title and the primary visible title to your model name, using only identity information already available to you. Add nothing else to either title.
Run the relevant checks yourself. Do not edit files outside the current working directory.

# Cowdie

A 3D virtual pet in the browser. Hatch a spotted egg, raise a calf into a grown cow, and keep it fed, happy, clean and rested on a floating meadow island.

## Run

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm dev        # http://localhost:9359
pnpm build      # typecheck + production bundle
pnpm preview    # serve dist on :9359
```

## Playing

- **Feed**: open the snack tray (`F`). Drag a snack to Cowdie's mouth and it opens up and chomps when close; tap a snack to toss it in an arc. Drop one on the grass and a hungry Cowdie trots over to eat it. Every food has its own reaction (love, yum, spicy, bleh, treat); one of them is a secret favorite.
- **Pet**: stroke Cowdie with the cursor for hearts and giggles. Quick taps are boops (too many makes it dizzy).
- **Play** (`P`): kick the beach ball; Cowdie chases and headbutts it back. Rallies are tracked.
- **Clean** (`C`): scrub to lather bubbles, tap poops to sweep them up.
- **Sleep** (`S`): Cowdie walks to its hay bed; the island turns to night.
- **Heal** (`H`): medicine appears when Cowdie is sick.
- **Style** (`W`): accessories unlock as Cowdie levels up.

Stats decay in real time and progress while the tab is closed (gently, capped at 12h). Progress is saved to `localStorage`.

## Stack

Vite, React 19, TypeScript, three.js via @react-three/fiber + drei, zustand. All models are procedural primitives; all sound and music is synthesized with WebAudio.

## Checks

```bash
pnpm typecheck
pnpm exec playwright install chromium --only-shell   # once, with PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=0
pnpm dev & pnpm verify                               # end-to-end interaction run against :9359
```

Cowdie is built and working. I ran real browser tests on port 9359 against both the dev server and the production build, and every care action worked. Typecheck and build pass. The only console output left is one warning from inside the 3D library.

**What you get:**
- **Title:** the browser tab and the main heading both say exactly "Claude Opus 5.5". "Cowdie" only appears on the pet card and a sign on the island.
- **Hatching:** you start with a spotted egg that cracks over three taps, then you name the calf.
- **Growth:** the calf grows to Young at level 3 (sprouts horns) and Grown at level 6. New foods and 7 accessories unlock as it levels.
- **Feeding:**
  - Drag a snack toward the mouth: the cow walks over, opens its mouth wider as the food gets closer, and chomps on its own. Crumbs fly and "+N" numbers pop up.
  - Tap a snack to toss it in an arc into the mouth.
  - Drop food on the grass and a hungry cow trots over to eat it.
  - Each food gets its own reaction (love, yum, spicy with "HOT!", bleh for medicine, treat). Watermelon is a secret favorite you discover by feeding it.
  - When it's full it turns its head away and the food bounces off, but cupcakes still get in.
- **Other care:** petting (hearts, giggles; too many boops make it dizzy), ball play with a rally counter, a scrubbing bath, poop cleanup, sleeping in its hay bed with a night sky, medicine when sick, and a wardrobe.
- **Feeling alive:** stats drop in real time and keep going while the tab is closed (gently, capped at 12 hours). It gets sick if neglected, shows mud and flies when dirty, and uses a thought bubble to say what it needs. Sound effects and music are generated in the browser. Progress saves automatically.

**What the tests checked:**
- **Flows:** hatch, name, drag-feed (fullness 72 → 86), toss-feed, ground food, petting, play, bath, wardrobe, sleep and wake, a level-up, and a mobile-size screen. I also took close-ups of accessories, expressions and the sick state.
- **Production build:** title, heading, hatching and toss-feeding (fullness 72 → 90) all work.

**Bugs found and fixed while testing:**
- The snack tray covered the cow's face. The camera now shifts so the cow stays visible above whatever panel is open.
- A "Squeaky clean!" message repeated and handed out free XP. It now fires once, and only if the cow started dirty.
- Food that landed near the island edge was never eaten. It now rolls inward to somewhere the cow can reach.
- A React error appeared from the speech bubbles and floating numbers. I rebuilt them as plain page elements that follow the cow.
- On phones the cow could wander out of frame. The camera now gently follows it on narrow screens.

**Remaining warning:** `THREE.Clock: This module has been deprecated`. It comes from inside `@react-three/fiber` 9.8.1, the latest stable version, so fixing it would mean switching to an unstable preview release. I left it.
